quote: More importantly, I realized that I had always known this—that the real memory had always been lurking in a corner of my mind
content: The technique does not depend on the memory being accurate. What the essay teaches is a present-tense skill — catch the flinch as it happens, not reconstruct one from childhood — and the childhood story is the occasion for naming it, which the essay presents as autobiography rather than as evidence. The reconstructive-memory literature is a good reason to distrust the details of the anecdote and no reason at all to distrust the existence of the swerve, which any reader can check the next time they notice themselves declining to finish a thought.

quote: Now I’m going to notice every time I do that, and clean out all my corners!
content: The essay is not claiming to catch suppression at its origin; it is claiming to catch the moment of turning away, which is available to introspection precisely because it happens before the content is gone. Anderson and Green's paradigm requires subjects to deliberately withhold retrieval on cue, which shows that the operation is one people can perform under instruction and therefore one they can notice performing (Anderson & Green 2001). On the label: the essay is describing motivated attention allocation, which is inside the standard scope of confirmation bias as biased search, and the review cited says so.
